newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico coffee exports extend record in 95-96 cycle.
newsitem.headline: Mexico coffee exports extend record in 95-96 cycle.

text.p: Mexican coffee exports dipped in August compared to August 1995, although exports to date in the October-September cycle are well over one million 60-kg bags against the same period last year, extending the previously set record.
The Mexican Coffee Council released figures Monday reporting that exports in August were 147,342 bags compared to 184,486 bags in August last year.
To date for the 1995-1996 cycle, exports between October and August have totaled 4,491,942 bags against the 3,155,877 bags exported in the same period in the 1994-1995 cycle.
As usual, the council gave no explanation of the figures, but it is well known that Mexico growers and traders have sold heavily this cycle for a number of reasons.

Mexico's crop was higher than expected, internal consumption dropped heavily and stocks have been whittled down so much that domestic roasters have called for permission to import 220,000 60-kg bags of cheap robustas to guarantee domestic demand.
The government is not expected to grant the import permits.
Also, growers sold early in the cycle to pay down debts with needed dollar incomes in the middle of Mexico's worst economic recession for decades and spiralling interest rates.
In the last October-September 1994-1995 cycle, Mexico exported a total of 3,257,774 60-kg bags.
-- Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com
